findings.title: compressed deictic day carries the prior scene
findings.claim: The deictic time word yawmaʾidhin makes the emergence occur on the already-framed day of the preceding upheaval rather than on an unspecified new date.
findings.mechanism: The temporal accusative and its recoverable omitted circumstance attach the marked day directly to yaṣduru, while the repeated opening frame from 99:4 carries the earthquake scene into this clause.
findings.reader_payoff: The first word makes the ayah feel like a continuation of an event already underway: the day now turns from earth's report to human movement.
findings.containment: The day reference remains a local temporal continuation; the supplied wider judgment-day parallels qualify the setting but do not replace the attachment to this emergence clause.

epistemic.reason: Both supplied records mark the temporal attachment and the carried-forward event frame as used, trusted evidence.

findings.title: judgment-day formula is locally specialized
findings.claim: The familiar judgment-day formula is locally specialized by its attachment to human emergence and the purpose of displaying deeds.
findings.mechanism: The supplied parallels identify a recognizable event-day formula, while the local adverbial attachment keeps that formula tied to yaṣduru and the following lām-led clause.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader hears a disclosure-day setting without losing sight of what this ayah specifically does on that day.
findings.containment: The recurrence supports the judgment setting, not a free-standing formula detached from this ayah's motion and disclosure sequence.

epistemic.reason: The trusted support marks the formula as narrowed because formal recurrence does not override its local syntactic attachment.

findings.title: opening word launches the when-what-why sequence
findings.claim: The opening time expression organizes the ayah as when, then what happens, then why it happens.
findings.mechanism: Its temporal attachment anchors the main emergence clause and prepares the later purpose clause, so the time expression functions as the first hinge of one ordered scene.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can follow the ayah's movement as a single sequence instead of three loosely adjacent statements.
findings.containment: The sequence describes this ayah's internal architecture and does not assert a wider surah-level thesis.

epistemic.reason: The supplied attachment and structural records are trusted and mark the when-what-why relation as used.

findings.title: intransitive emergence starts an agency arc
findings.claim: The intransitive Form I verb yaṣduru first presents the people as grammatical movers before the purpose clause makes them recipients of display.
findings.mechanism: Al-nāsu is the subject of the active imperfect motion verb, and the later passive yuraw shifts the same participants into the patient role of disclosure.
findings.reader_payoff: The grammar itself lets the reader feel movement followed by a loss of control over what must be seen.
findings.containment: The verb remains an intransitive outward-emergence form; the later passive contrast adds the agency arc without changing the ordinary motion.

epistemic.reason: The QAC, verb-instance, and attachment records are trusted and explicitly support the active-to-passive contrast.

findings.title: rare finite verb continues hidden-to-visible movement
findings.claim: The marked finite use of yaṣduru continues the packet's hidden-to-visible movement into public human emergence.
findings.mechanism: The exact finite form is rare in the supplied profile, and the same-surah boundary evidence connects it to the preceding concealed command and earth's reporting before visible human motion.
findings.reader_payoff: Humanity enters as what was previously held within the scene becomes publicly present.
findings.containment: Rarity and the boundary rows qualify the contextual coloring; they do not turn the verb into a different tense, voice, or causal form.

epistemic.reason: The trusted contextual and boundary records mark this finite use and its hidden-to-visible connection as used.

findings.title: sound texture reinforces outward release
findings.claim: The consonant texture of yaṣduru reinforces the sense of compact outward release.
findings.mechanism: The supplied phonetic and variant records concern the actual local verb and make its emphatic ṣād, dental dāl, and rolling r feel forceful while preserving the Form I intransitive parse.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can hear the emergence as a short, pressed release without treating sound as a replacement for grammar.
findings.containment: Sound corroborates the outward-motion image; it does not independently create a new lexical sense or alter the standard reading.

epistemic.reason: The trusted phonetic records explicitly mark the sound contribution as reinforcing the local verb.

findings.title: source-exit image adds exposure pressure
findings.claim: The source, chest, and front associations color yaṣduru as release from containment and add pressure toward exposure.
findings.mechanism: The finite verb still selects outward issuing, but its supplied root field meets the preceding hidden-to-visible movement and makes emergence feel like contents leaving a source or front.
findings.reader_payoff: The ordinary meaning of emerging gains an exposed edge: what comes out is becoming available to public view.
findings.containment: This is root pressure around the finite verb, not an explicit chest noun, source noun, or causative construction; the ordinary outward-emergence sense stays intact.

epistemic.reason: The trusted support retains the source/chest associations only as narrowed background coloring under the local valency.

findings.title: one human noun anchors later plural references

findings.mechanism: The attachment evidence makes the plural patient of yuraw and the possessive suffix of aʿmālahum refer back to the people named by al-nāsu.
findings.reader_payoff: The scene does not change participants between moving out, being shown, and owning the displayed actions.
findings.containment: The finding establishes grammatical continuity of reference; it does not infer anything beyond the supplied subject and possessive attachments.

epistemic.reason: The trusted attachment records explicitly support the common human antecedent and possessive relation.

findings.title: collective humanity prepares individual accounting

findings.mechanism: The supplied same-surah comparison places the collective subject here between the singular human voice earlier and the distributive atom-weight clauses in 99:7-8.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can feel the scale change from one named human collective to personal accounting without losing the continuity of the scene.
findings.containment: The finding describes a supplied local-to-next-ayah progression; it does not import a broader surah architecture or sort the people into outcomes here.

epistemic.reason: The trusted same-surah comparison marks the collective-to-distributive movement as used.

findings.title: definite collective names humanity as subject
findings.claim: The definite nominative al-nāsu names humanity as the known collective subject of the emergence clause, rather than an arbitrary group.
findings.mechanism: The definite prefix and nominative subject attachment give yaṣduru a generic human subject, and the judgment setting supports that universal human scope.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader hears the people as the whole human field entering the scene, not as a locally selected crowd.
findings.containment: Definiteness and generic scope establish the subject's reference; they do not independently specify every individual outcome.

epistemic.reason: The trusted QAC, subject, and contextual records mark the definite human collective as used.

findings.title: human profile is enriched, not redefined

findings.mechanism: The supplied derivational discussion colors the definite collective with a human profile, while the local noun and grammar continue to mean the human collective as subject.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can sense human vulnerability and social life in the participants without turning an etymological dispute into a second dictionary meaning asserted as fact.
findings.containment: The derivational background remains qualified and subordinate to the local collective noun; it does not activate every related sense or replace the ordinary subject.

epistemic.reason: The trusted support preserves a valid derivational dispute and explicitly narrows it to enrichment rather than a separate local sense.

findings.title: humanity enters after the earth-focused arc
findings.claim: The definite human subject hands the scene from earth as witness to humanity as the public bearer of consequence.
findings.mechanism: The supplied boundary rows close the earlier earth-pronoun chain at the point where al-nāsu enters, and the local subject then carries the judgment-field relations into movement and display.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader sees who now occupies the foreground: the earth has reported, and humanity has entered the disclosed scene.

epistemic.reason: The trusted boundary and co-occurrence records mark the earth-to-human handoff as used.

findings.title: clipped consonants sound the separation

findings.mechanism: The phonetic record is tied to the actual circumstantial noun, whose clipped consonant pattern echoes the divided state already carried by its syntax and lexical sense.

findings.title: scattered state bridges motion to deed display
findings.claim: Ashtātan is the middle state that connects outward emergence to the later display of deeds.
findings.mechanism: Its circumstantial position between yaṣduru and the purpose clause turns separation into the intermediate condition through which a collective becomes distributed for accountability.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader sees fragmentation as the hinge between coming out and having one's actions displayed.
findings.containment: The supplied echoes corroborate this bridge, while the local noun remains a state of emergence rather than an independently narrated scattering act.

epistemic.reason: The trusted word-analysis and supplied echo rows mark the structural bridge as used.

findings.title: accusative state tells how people emerge

findings.containment: The finding is limited to the supplied circumstantial parse; it does not deny the word's lexical separation image or add an expressed scatterer.

findings.title: indefinite plural leaves the dispersal open-ended

epistemic.reason: The trusted morphological and contextual records mark the indefinite plural distribution as used.

findings.title: rare nominal form foregrounds state, not a scatterer
findings.claim: The marked nominal form foregrounds fragmentation as the state visible during emergence rather than narrating a separate act by an expressed scatterer.
findings.mechanism: The supplied rarity and nominal-form evidence makes the condition itself prominent, while the absence of a local verbal scatterer keeps the focus on how the people appear.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader feels the markedness of being scattered without inventing an agent or a second clause.
findings.containment: The source supports a qualified form effect; it does not erase the ordinary separation meaning or prove that no causal force lies behind the scene.

epistemic.reason: The trusted support explicitly narrows the rare nominal form to a visible state rather than a finite scattering event.

findings.title: scattering breaks a gathered collective into accountable units
findings.claim: The separation sense of ashtātan breaks the named human collective into differentiated units prepared for accountability.
findings.mechanism: The word's supplied scattering/separation field meets its circumstantial position after al-nāsu and before the purpose clause, so collective emergence becomes distributed disclosure.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader sees the collective being opened into separate groupings before the deeds are shown.
findings.containment: The separation deepens the ordinary scattered-groups reading; it does not select a moral winner or replace the circumstantial state parse.

findings.title: structural hinge supplies the ayah's why
findings.claim: The lām-led clause supplies the ayah's why: the emergence is oriented toward the display of deeds.
findings.mechanism: The purpose particle attaches the following passive verb to the main emergence clause, turning the sequence from setting and movement into an explained action.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader understands why the people issue forth instead of receiving the display as an unrelated next event.

findings.claim: The proclitic li- makes the dependency between emergence and display visible and audible as one tight unit.

findings.title: purpose particle governs the display verb
findings.claim: The purpose particle governs the subjunctive passive display verb, so displaying deeds is the goal of emergence rather than a merely coordinated later event.

findings.title: active emergence turns into passive disclosure
findings.claim: The grammar moves from active human emergence to passive human reception of disclosure.

findings.reader_payoff: Humanity moves into the scene, then meets an accountability event it does not grammatically control.

epistemic.reason: The trusted voice and attachment records explicitly mark the active-to-passive shift as used.

findings.title: Form IV passive makes people recipients of display
findings.claim: The Form IV passive makes the people recipients of a caused display rather than controllers of the seeing.
findings.mechanism: The passive plural subjunctive is governed by the purpose lām, with al-nāsu controlling the patient role; the showing agent is left unspoken while the display remains imposed.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader feels accountability as something made visible to the people, not merely as an act they choose to perform.
findings.containment: The suppressed agent is not separately named here; the finding stays with caused display and does not add an unsupported agent to the surface grammar.

epistemic.reason: The trusted QAC and verb-instance records explicitly establish the Form IV passive and patient relation.

findings.title: passive display anticipates active seeing in 99:7-8
findings.claim: The passive display in this ayah prepares the supplied progression to active individual seeing in 99:7-8.
findings.mechanism: The standard passive yuraw places the collective in a received display, while the supplied following forms use active yarah for each person's later witnessing.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can follow accountability from a collective disclosure imposed on the people to each doer's active encounter with the smallest deed.
findings.containment: The progression is limited to the supplied neighboring ayahs and keeps the standard passive parse; it does not turn the local passive into active agency.

epistemic.reason: The trusted comparison records mark the passive-to-active progression as used while preserving the standard parse.

findings.title: purpose verb resolves the motion sequence
findings.claim: The purpose verb resolves the motion sequence by making emergence lead toward display, and its imperfect form audibly pairs it with the earlier motion verb.
findings.mechanism: The purpose attachment gives yuraw the role of destination for yaṣduru, while the two imperfect forms create a spoken pairing of movement and disclosure.
findings.reader_payoff: The two verbs sound like linked stages of one event rather than unrelated actions.
findings.containment: The sound pairing supports the syntactic purpose relation; it does not create a new voice or change the ordinary meaning of either verb.

epistemic.reason: The trusted attachment and sound records mark the purpose resolution and pairing as used.

findings.title: seeing becomes evidentiary apprehension
findings.claim: The seeing verb becomes apprehension of evidence because its direct object is the people's deeds.
findings.mechanism: The object aʿmālahum supplies accountable content for the caused seeing, so the display includes recognition of what the record means rather than bare passage before eyesight.
findings.reader_payoff: The shown deeds can be understood as evidence that must be faced, not only as images that happen to appear.
findings.containment: The wider opinion and dream-vision branches remain unselected; this qualified finding stays with display plus recognition supplied by the object.

epistemic.reason: The trusted support narrows the perception field to display and recognition in contact with the deeds object.

findings.title: final phrase audibly lands on possessed deeds
findings.claim: The final phrase aʿmālahum audibly lands the ayah on deeds gathered under the people's ownership.
findings.mechanism: The plural object closes the purpose clause and the possessive suffix binds it to the same human participants, while the supplied phonetic row marks the closure.
findings.reader_payoff: The scene settles on owned deeds as its final object before the following ayahs break them down.
findings.containment: The audible closure reinforces the grammatical object and possessive relation; it does not add a moral verdict not yet stated here.

epistemic.reason: The trusted final-position and phonetic records mark the possessed-deeds landing as used.

findings.title: plural record forwards into individual atom-weight accounting
findings.claim: The plural record in this ayah forwards into the individual atom-weight accounting of 99:7-8.
findings.mechanism: The same deed root returns in the supplied following clauses, where the plural object gives way to whoever does even an atom's weight, creating a zoom from collective record to each deed.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader sees why the plural record can still reach every tiny act.
findings.containment: The transition is limited to the supplied following ayahs; this ayah itself presents the collective owned record without yet dividing its outcomes.

epistemic.reason: The trusted same-root and next-ayah records mark the collective-to-atom movement as used.

findings.title: deeds imply accountable doing without yet sorting outcomes
findings.claim: Aʿmālahum denotes accountable intentional doing while leaving the moral sorting of those deeds open at this point.
findings.mechanism: The supplied primary branch centers intentional work and allows good and bad action, but the local plural noun carries no good-or-evil qualifier; the following ayahs supply that sorting.

findings.containment: The candidate remains a qualified action-field reading; it does not assign a moral outcome to any deed within 99:6.

epistemic.reason: The trusted support explicitly narrows the action field to intentional doing without importing later good/evil sorting.

findings.title: owned deeds are the object shown
findings.claim: The deeds shown are owned by the same people who emerge.
findings.mechanism: Attachment evidence marks aʿmālahum as the direct object of yuraw and the suffix as a possessive genitive tied to the human subject.
findings.reader_payoff: Accountability lands on each people's own deeds rather than on an anonymous archive.
findings.containment: The finding establishes ownership and objecthood; it does not yet classify the deeds as good or evil.

epistemic.reason: The trusted attachment records explicitly support the direct-object and possessive relations.

findings.title: shown deeds may confront self-assessment
findings.claim: When the owned deeds are displayed, the record can confront a person's self-assessment as a qualified live implication.
findings.mechanism: The supplied cross-reference uses displayed deeds to expose mistaken self-assessment, and the local object relation provides the point of contact while 99:6 itself only states that the deeds are shown.
findings.reader_payoff: The disclosure remains capable of surprise or reversal instead of being reduced to a record that merely confirms what the doer already thought.
findings.containment: The supplied cross-reference qualifies a possible consequence of display; it does not assert that surprise or reversal is the only event in this ayah.

epistemic.reason: The trusted support explicitly narrows the implication because the local ayah states display without describing the reaction.

findings.title: baseline_departure_after_arrival
findings.claim: The attributed trace can be heard as humanity leaving a common station after arrival, separating into cohorts, and reaching disclosure of its own intentional acts.
findings.mechanism: The focus sequence joins yaṣduru's departure, al-nāsu, ashtātan, the purpose lām with yuraw, and aʿmālahum; the supplied HFT trace attributes the after-arrival movement and makes passive disclosure its endpoint.
findings.reader_payoff: The motion becomes a release from a shared point whose destination is accountable self-disclosure, not dispersal alone.
findings.containment: This is retained as attributed HFT evidence because the reader identity is legacy-unbound. The ordinary reading remains people emerging in scattered groups so their deeds are shown, and no water scene is asserted beyond the supplied trace.

epistemic.reason: The exact focus anchor and branch trace are supplied, but the reader identity is legacy-unbound, so the compound remains qualified and attributed.

findings.title: baseline_social_unmaking
findings.claim: The attributed social trace turns dispersal into separation of once-familiar human parties whose dealings are made visible.
findings.mechanism: The supplied trace links familiarity, distance, mutual visibility, and reciprocal dealings across al-nāsu, ashtātan, yuraw, and aʿmālahum, changing a private-file picture into relational consequence.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can see separated parties confronting the dealings through which their members affected one another.
findings.containment: This remains an attributed local social overlay. It deepens the spatial scattering and does not claim that every displayed deed is interpersonal.

epistemic.reason: The exact focus anchor and trace are supplied, but the reader identity is legacy-unbound; the social mechanism is therefore qualified and attributed.

branch_activations.branch_gloss: yabancılık duymadan yakınlık ve rahatlık hissetme
branch_activations.facet_statement: Bir kişi ya da şey karşısında yabancılık ve ürkme duygusunun kalkıp yakınlık, rahatlık veya sevinç oluşmasını anlatır.
branch_activations.carrier: The human noun carries familiarity, nearness, and relief from estrangement.
branch_activations.independent_trigger: The scattered-state and mutual-display words supply the undoing of that familiarity.
branch_activations.activation: The attributed trace lets the once-familiar collective meet separation and confrontation.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: A known human collective is opened into parties whose former nearness is no longer shelter.
branch_activations.boundary: The social-familiarity facet is attributed; the ordinary human-collective reading remains present.

branch_activations.facet_statement: İki tarafın karşılaşıp birbirini görmesi.
branch_activations.carrier: The passive seeing form carries the relation of parties appearing before one another.
branch_activations.independent_trigger: The human collective and separated-group carriers create distinct parties that can face one another.
branch_activations.activation: The attributed trace turns caused display into a confrontation structure between separated parties.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: The separated groups are made to face what becomes visible between them.
branch_activations.boundary: The branch supplies mutual visibility, not a claim that the local verb is an active reciprocal form.

branch_activations.branch_gloss: iki şey arasındaki büyük uzaklık ve uyuşmazlık
branch_activations.facet_statement: İki şey arasındaki uzaklığın veya ayrılığın çok büyük olduğu bildirilir.
branch_activations.carrier: The circumstantial noun carries great distance and separation between parties.
branch_activations.independent_trigger: The definite human subject and the relational deeds object provide the parties and what connects them.
branch_activations.activation: The attributed trace makes the dispersed state a social distance rather than only a spatial distribution.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: The human collective appears as distinct parties placed apart for disclosure.
branch_activations.boundary: The distance facet remains a supplied social overlay; the ordinary scattered-group state is retained.

branch_activations.facet_statement: Bir kişiyle karşılıklı işlem yürütme ana anlamdır.
branch_activations.carrier: The deeds noun carries reciprocal dealings between people.
branch_activations.independent_trigger: The human subject and caused-display verb make those dealings the object brought into view.
branch_activations.activation: The attributed trace attaches the displayed work field to the relations that connected or divided the parties.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: The displayed record includes the dealings through which separated people affected one another.
branch_activations.boundary: The reciprocal-dealings facet is attributed and does not replace the broader owned-deeds reading.

findings.title: outlier_water_station_echo
findings.claim: An attributed, form-distant lexical echo lets the focus picture people leaving a watering station and meeting their acts as provision that satisfies or fails to satisfy.
findings.mechanism: The supplied trace joins yaṣduru's departure-after-arrival branch with the non-dominant split-root water branches at the focus seeing form and keeps the echo attached to the actual deeds object.
findings.reader_payoff: The ordinary display of deeds gains a second local picture: what people carry into disclosure can be experienced as provision that reveals whether satisfaction has been reached.
findings.containment: This is an exploratory, form-distant echo under the packet's non-dominant split-root mapping. It never replaces the dominant seeing/display reading of yuraw and adds no literal water noun to the ayah.

epistemic.reason: The exact HFT outlier is supplied with an exploratory confidence and legacy-unbound provenance; its non-dominant split-root mapping requires an attributed boundary.

branch_activations.facet_statement: Daha önce varılan bir yerden veya girilen bir durumdan ayrılıp geri yönelmeyi belirtir.
branch_activations.carrier: The finite verb yaṣduru carries departure from a previously reached point.
branch_activations.independent_trigger: The seeing/display form and the deeds object supply the destination that follows departure.
branch_activations.activation: The attributed trace lets departure after arrival frame the disclosure scene as leaving a shared watering station.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: People leave a watering station and move into the display of their deeds.
branch_activations.boundary: The watering station is an attributed lexical echo; the focus does not name water.

branch_activations.facet_statement: Temel durum, susuzluğun su içme sonucunda sona ermesi ve kişinin suya kanmasıdır.
branch_activations.carrier: The focus seeing form is assigned the supplied water-satisfaction branch.
branch_activations.independent_trigger: The departure verb and the owned-deeds object give the satisfaction image a local before-and-after contact.
branch_activations.activation: The attributed non-dominant branch meets the departure and deeds carriers, recasting what is encountered after leaving the station as possible satisfaction.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: The displayed encounter can be felt as provision that satisfies or leaves satisfaction unresolved.
branch_activations.boundary: This water-satisfaction branch is form-distant and non-dominant; the ordinary caused-seeing sense remains intact.

branch_activations.facet_statement: Çekirdek eylem, başkalarının kullanması için su çekip onlara getirmektir.
branch_activations.carrier: The focus seeing form is assigned the supplied branch of fetching water for others.
branch_activations.independent_trigger: The departure verb identifies those who leave, and the deeds object identifies what is carried into the disclosure contact.
branch_activations.activation: The attributed water-fetching branch lets the display object be imagined cautiously as provision brought for those departing.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: The people's deeds can be pictured as what is carried toward the departing group as provision.
branch_activations.boundary: The fetching image is attributed and form-distant; it is not a claim that a literal water-carrying action is grammatically present.

branch_activations.facet_statement: Bir yapanın bilerek ortaya koyduğu iş veya eylem anlamı çekirdektir.
branch_activations.carrier: The plural noun aʿmālahum carries intentional acts and produced work.
branch_activations.independent_trigger: The departure and water-satisfaction contacts make those acts the object encountered after leaving the station.
branch_activations.activation: The attributed trace keeps the water echo attached to the actual disclosed object rather than floating free as scenery.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: What is encountered after departure is the people's own intentional activity, experienced within the water-provision echo.
branch_activations.boundary: The ordinary owned-deeds object remains the anchor; the water image adds no moral verdict.

findings.title: outlier_deeds_as_traveled_routes
findings.claim: An attributed exploratory overlay makes the owned deeds appear as divergent roads worn by action, with the departing parties as travelers.
findings.mechanism: The supplied trace joins departure, distance, the work-branch of an open traveled road, the branch of walking travelers, and caused seeing, so the object of disclosure becomes a route-shaped image.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can perceive deeds as courses that have been made durable by repeated walking while still seeing them as the owned actions displayed.
findings.containment: The route image is a metaphor generated by the attributed branch convergence, not the syntax of the object phrase. The ordinary scattered emergence and display of deeds remain recoverable.

epistemic.reason: The exact HFT outlier is exploratory and legacy-unbound; its route image is retained with the supplied metaphorical boundary.

branch_activations.facet_statement: Daha önce varılan bir yerden veya girilen bir durumdan ayrılıp geri yönelmeyi belirtir.
branch_activations.carrier: The finite verb yaṣduru carries departure from a reached point.
branch_activations.independent_trigger: The scattered-state word and purpose lām give the departure divergent courses and a directed destination.
branch_activations.activation: The attributed trace turns the outward motion into the starting movement of travelers on separate routes.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: The separated people depart along courses that lead into disclosure.
branch_activations.boundary: The route overlay remains attributed; yaṣduru still ordinarily means to issue forth.

branch_activations.branch_gloss: iki şey arasındaki büyük uzaklık ve uyuşmazlık
branch_activations.facet_statement: İki şey arasındaki uzaklığın veya ayrılığın çok büyük olduğu bildirilir.
branch_activations.carrier: The circumstantial noun carries great distance and separation.
branch_activations.independent_trigger: The departure verb and deeds object supply the movement and what the routes disclose.
branch_activations.activation: The attributed distance facet turns scattered groups into parties taking divergent courses.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: The people emerge as travelers separated onto distinct routes.
branch_activations.boundary: The distance facet does not erase the ordinary dispersed-state parse.

branch_activations.facet_statement: Bir şeyi başkasına gösterip onun görmesini sağlama.
branch_activations.carrier: The passive seeing form carries making the object visible to the people.
branch_activations.independent_trigger: The departure and deeds carriers identify the route image's movement and object.
branch_activations.activation: The attributed display branch keeps the route overlay subordinate to the explicit act of showing deeds.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: The travelers are made to see the courses their deeds have made visible.
branch_activations.boundary: The showing relation is retained; no active reciprocal seeing is added.

branch_activations.facet_statement: Yürünmüş ve işlek hale gelmiş yol ana anlamdır.
branch_activations.carrier: The deeds noun is assigned the supplied collocation of an open, well-worn road.
branch_activations.independent_trigger: Departure and separated groups supply travelers and divergent movement.
branch_activations.activation: The attributed road branch meets the owned-deeds carrier, making repeated action legible as a course worn into the world.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: The people's deeds appear as open roads made durable by what has been done.
branch_activations.boundary: The road collocation is an attributed overlay, not the literal lexical gloss of the plural object.

branch_activations.facet_statement: Yolculuk eden kişilerin yaya gitmesi ana anlamdır.
branch_activations.carrier: The deeds noun is assigned the supplied collocation of people traveling on foot.
branch_activations.independent_trigger: The departure and scattered-state carriers supply the travelers and their separated movement.
branch_activations.activation: The attributed walking-traveler branch lets the human parties be pictured as people moving along the courses made by their actions.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: The departing parties appear as walkers whose own deeds form the routes before them.
branch_activations.boundary: The walking-traveler collocation is attributed and does not change the ordinary human subject or owned-deeds object.

friction_notes: All four assigned HFT records are legacy_unbound; their exact focus traces are retained as attributed activations rather than independently adjudicated lexical findings.
The non-dominant split-root water trace is retained only as an exploratory, form-distant lexical echo because the focus seeing-form's dominant mapping is separate.
The packet supplies no selected context units or connection records, so all retained activations are focus-local and no context landing is claimed.
The packet supplies no staged reader responses or reader-walk records; discovery does not infer any missing before/after reader result.
The five QAC root-occurrence rows are ledger-only provenance and are explicitly rejected as standalone findings.
